name: Battle of Vesuvius
intro: Near Mount Vesuvius, at a place called Veseris, 340 BC. The Latins, Rome’s allies, have risen against her. They fight with the same arms and order as the Romans. You are the consuls Titus Manlius Torquatus and Publius Decius Mus.
debrief: In Livy’s account, Manlius forbade single combats; when his own son fought and killed a Latin champion, Manlius had him executed. Both consuls dreamed that one side would lose its general and the other its army. When the Roman left gave way, Decius devoted himself and the enemy to the gods below and charged to his death. Manlius held back his triarii until the Latins had committed their last line, then sent them in fresh, and the Latins were crushed. The dream and the speeches belong to legend, but the victory ended the Latin League. The other choices are what-ifs.

win: The triarii rise and go in.
lose: The Latin triarii break your last line.

decisions.title: Brothers in arms
decisions.text: The Latins, Rome’s old allies, have risen. They fight exactly as Romans do, with the same arms and the same ranks. You are the consuls Titus Manlius Torquatus and Publius Decius Mus.

hint.text: In a fight between twins, discipline will decide.

scout.text: Forbid any man to fight outside the ranks, on pain of death.

choices.label: Forbid any fighting outside the ranks

fx.text: The order goes out: no man leaves the line to fight a Latin. The army knows you mean it.

choices.label: Let the bravest win glory in single combats

fx.text: The duels are brave, and the line grows ragged.

choices.label: Offer the Latins a share of power to end it

fx.text: The Latins want more than Rome will give.

decisions.title: The consul’s son
decisions.text: The young Titus Manlius, your son, was challenged by a Latin horseman, broke your order and killed him. He comes proudly to show you the spoils.

scout.text: If the order means nothing for the consul’s son, it means nothing for anyone.

choices.label: Have him executed for breaking the order

fx.text: The young man is executed in front of the army. No one will break ranks again. The army is horrified, and obeys.

choices.label: Pardon him: the army loves him for his courage

fx.text: The army cheers, and takes note that orders can be bent.

choices.label: Praise him and give him a command

fx.text: Other young men look for duels.

decisions.title: The dream
decisions.text: Both consuls dream the same dream: one army must lose its general, and the other side its whole host. The left wing, under Decius, is giving way.

hint.text: The left is buckling under the Latin right.

scout.text: A consul can devote himself and the enemy to the gods of the underworld, and charge to his death.

fx.text: Decius recites the old prayer, veiled, and rides alone into the Latin ranks. He is killed, and the Latins near him lose heart.

choices.label: Send the reserves from the centre to the left

fx.text: The centre thins to save the left.

choices.label: Let the left fall back and shorten the line

decisions.title: The reserve
decisions.text: The Latins have thrown in their triarii, thinking your last line is spent. Your own triarii are still kneeling behind the standards.

hint.text: The Latin front ranks are exhausted.

scout.text: Hold your triarii until the Latins have nothing left, then send them in fresh.

choices.label: Keep the triarii kneeling a little longer

fx.text: Your triarii wait, kneeling, while the Latins spend themselves.

choices.label: Send the triarii in now to meet theirs

fx.text: Fresh meets fresh, and neither gives.

choices.label: Pull the whole army back toward the camp

fx.text: The retreat is hard to stop.

decisions.title: Fresh men
decisions.text: The Latins are worn out. Their last line has been thrown in. Yours is fresh.

hint.text: Nothing is left behind the Latin line.

choices.label: Send the fresh triarii through the line

fx.text: Your triarii rise and go through the tired ranks into the Latins. The Latins break; three-quarters of them are killed or taken.

choices.label: Send the horse round their flank to finish them

fx.text: The horse charge the Latin flank and it begins to give.
